touches.text: Test tiers: commit, hourly, daily and weekly. Each tier runs only what it must, so a commit needs only its own proofs and the long runs wait for the long tiers; nothing runs just in case.

Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead.

A red is first a question: is the code wrong, or is the tooth measuring the wrong thing? An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6, because even the Laws rest finally on the core principles. Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6). A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8).
A proof that cannot go red without its build (its hollow is empty) stands only on Akien's answered approval, recorded as the hollow reading and re-read at clearance; any other empty hollow is red.
A request seen before is answered from the stored answer, if it still holds, and the host is not touched. That untouched call is compilation.

The stored answers are learning, so they live in the memory model: a tree the proxy holds by the librarian's delegation, asking "what did this request answer?". An answer is found by its exact request and carries no embedding (4.3.1.6). The meter (every call, its verdict and cost) is not learning: it is metrics (17.27). The inference ticket, a file in the logs tree on the 30 day clock, is only for debugging.

The memory model. Everything Cairn keeps as LEARNING in database memory is these five things, and only these. Logs, troubles, git records and a device's own state keep their own homes (4.3.2-4.3.4). WHY: one kind of access everywhere.
Trees as tables, permanent: each asks one question, with the weights in its leaves. A tree past 5K leaves is calved at its dominant attractors, a deterministic code shear.

Commit: the proofs of the component the ticket changed, since RULE 1 bounds a change to its component. Passing them puts the component in service, yellow: proven where it changed, not yet measured against what depends on it. In service needs only the best we can do now: 80% trust.

The ticket IS its own manager. It carries its workflow and status, and asks each gate whether it can transit. If refused, it gets itself back to design for fixing. If no handler is available to ask, it throws a trouble and waits until we decide. Design is CC and Akien until the outline is implemented; a design agent comes after that. Until then a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, which both read when a session opens, and nothing posts to a design verb that no machine answers.

Trees as tables, temporary: made for one activity and dropped after it. Two kinds so far: a working tree that sleep builds while consolidating and does not need afterwards, and config read from disk and held in the db. For config the file on disk stays the source: the tree is derived from it, rebuilt when the file changes, never edited in place.

Lifetimes. Each tree declares its lifetime when it is made: kept, one activity (eg one sleep run), or until its source file changes. Dropping a tree drops its leaves and its own links. A node goes only when no tree indexes it, so whatever a temporary tree's activity promoted into a permanent tree outlives it. The drop is enforced, not a habit. WHY: a run that ends without dropping its tables leaves them behind forever.

The yield report (tokens spent against tokens saved, the meter for Telos 1) reads the metrics table (17.27): each call records its spent, saved and latency rows under the call as subject, kept forever, so the all-time total is a sum. WHY: inference tickets are only for debugging, so they are no metric.

metric: records a measurement of anything. WHY: a metric is a primitive; its job is to measure whatever it is, and like feedback (which a metric strictly is) it must eventually have a consumer. USERS: any probe or tool.

Metrics land in one table so any metric can be reported fast from one place: at, name, source (the device/tool that recorded it), start, end, value, unit, subject (the thing measured), info (json). Fields not relevant to a source stay blank. Indexed on name and source by time. One thing (eg an inference call) may record several metrics in its short life, sharing one subject.

conflicts.ticket_says: Find why the proof reds and fix it so the proof reseals green, addressing failures: (1) live_the_table_is_gone_and_the_meter_carried showing 224 leaves in the answer tree, and (2) every_other_proof_under_the_device_stays_green finding another proof red
conflicts.why: Per 9.4.2.3.7.6, when a red is diagnosed, 'Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act.' The second failing tooth (every_other_proof_under_the_device_stays_green) may be measuring the wrong thing or may be invalid as written (since it's failing due to a pre-existing or external red). If the fix removes or modifies this tooth, that decision must be recorded. The ticket does not state whether this tooth is being changed, nor does it carry a decision for such a change. If built as written without this determination, the clause is violated.

conflicts.ticket_says: The proof reseals green by fixing the proxy code, while one of its own teeth finds another proof (test_the_proxy_stands_at_its_outline_address.py) is red
conflicts.why: Per 9.4.2.3.7.5, 'Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed.' The failing tooth every_other_proof_under_the_device_stays_green has found a red in another proof. The ticket claims only to fix the main proof file. If that other proof's red is caused by the proxy code (related to the work), it must be fixed in this ticket or the main proof's tooth will not pass. If it is unrelated, it must be ticketed separately. The ticket does not address which is true or how the dependency will be satisfied. If built as written without resolving this, the main proof cannot reseal green (its own tooth prevents it), or every red is not addressed.
